question: Can Beijing prevent Europe from conducting investigations? On 19 August 2026, the Chinese authorities ordered organisations and individuals under their jurisdiction not to cooperate with some parts of the Commission’s investigation into the proposed acquisition of Ceconomy by the Chinese group JD.com.

Beijing said that the investigation constituted ‘unlawful extraterritorial jurisdiction measures’ and threatened the EU with countermeasures. In its investigation, the Commission is focusing in particular on potential Chinese subsidies that may have distorted competition in the context of the acquisition. 1.
Does the Commission take the view that the measures taken by the Chinese authorities are likely to hinder its investigation in practice?

What legal and practical action can the Commission take to pursue its investigation effectively when the authorities of a third country order companies and individuals under their jurisdiction not to cooperate?

Does the Commission believe that the EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation provides it with the means it needs to act in situations like these, and is it considering tightening up the regulation if necessary?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.10.2026) Under the Foreign Subsidies Regulation (FSR)1, the Commission enjoys a range of investigative powers, including the possibility of requesting information from companies under investigation. These powers are complemented by fines and penalty payments if companies fail to provide the requested information or supply incomplete, incorrect, or misleading information.

In addition, pursuant to Article 16 of the FSR, if a company fails to cooperate with the investigation, the Commission may take a decision based on the facts available. Article 16(3) of the FSR notably allows the Commission to assume that a foreign financial contribution conferred a benefit to a non-cooperating company.

In practice, the FSR gives companies an incentive to cooperate and provide the information required. While the Commission cannot comment on ongoing investigations, it has already applied Article 16 of the FSR in its past decisional practice and will continue to do so whenever necessary.
The Review Report2 published by the Commission in July 2026 confirmed that the FSR has been successful in capturing high-risk concentrations.
1 Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on foreign
subsidies distorting the internal market, OJ L 330, 23.12.2022, pp. 1–45. 2 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026DC0368.
